From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly Signal: ops checkpoint & QBR asks

Good morning team — quick, focused update for this week (wins / risks / asks). I'm attaching the updated QBR playbook for reference. TL;DR in the asks section.

WINS:
- Dedicated capacity pilot with DeltaRetail completed performance baseline; tail latency down 18% vs last month.
- Cost-savings experiment (aggressive KV cache TTL) reduced token spend on a sample workload by ~9%.
- Onboarded NorthStar (inference partner) for marketplace integration; initial test calls are green.

RISKS / NOTABLE HEADWINDS:
- Model-serving pressure: two enterprise customers expect sustained 2x traffic in Nov; current Dedicated pools show slot saturation risk for long sequences. See Jonas' note below.
- QBR deck gaps: still missing the SLA exception justification (legal needs the ask formalized).
- Procurement lead times for additional A100 capacity look like 8–10 weeks if we need hardware in-region.

ASKS / ACTIONS (priority ordering):
1) Jonas — run capacity stress test using expected Nov traffic profile and proposal for temporary routing to hosted (fallback) by EOD Thu. (Attachment: QBR_playbook_v2.pdf)
2) Laura — prep a 1-slide SLA exception justification for the QBR describing compensating controls; I can route to Legal once drafted by Wed COB.
3) Karthik — confirm whether we can compress model variants (medium quant) without quality regression for DeltaRetail by next Tue; if yes, present quick rollback plan.
4) Soojin/Markus — draft a short contingency runbook for routing/auto-fallback for client-facing SLOs; one pager preferred.

Notes: I flagged procurement (cc'd below) for early engagement; if we need to accelerate capacity, we should decide by next Friday.

Attachments: QBR_playbook_v2.pdf, SLA_exception_request.docx

Thanks — short replies appreciated with owners noted.

— Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly Signal: ops checkpoint & QBR asks

Running the capacity probes now (using the Nov forecast: 2.1x session count, 1.8x avg sequence length). Early results: slot contention appears when long-token requests (>4k) align with peak windows; horizontal autoscale reacts but with a 45–90s cold start window causing SLO blips.

Mitigation options (short list):
- Short-term: auto-fallback routing to hosted (warm pool) for long sequences during peak windows; requires policy flag and QoS header — 3 workdays dev effort + config.
- Medium-term: proactive scaling of Dedicated pools by adding 2 nodes in US-west (procurement + infra timeline ~8 weeks).
- Alternative: request clients to enforce max_sequence via negotiation (business ask) — low engineering effort, needs sales alignment.

I'll deliver a technical proposal with config snippets and a failback test plan by Thursday COB as requested. If team wants the short-term routing, we need signoff from Product & Sales by Wed EOD.

— Jonas
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
(Attachment stub: stress-probe-summary.csv)
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-insights.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly Signal: ops checkpoint & QBR asks

Appreciate the heads up; Acme's projection is aggressive but accurate for our holiday campaign. We prefer the short-term routing option to avoid throttles — our product team can accept a temporary hosted fallback during peak hours if you flag it as a best-effort SLO and provide post-mortem guarantees.

Two asks from our side:
1) Visibility: can we get a health webhook for requests that are routed to hosted so we can instrument retries client-side?
2) Communication: we need a draft customer notice (one paragraph) explaining fallback behavior and expected recovery timeline — can you share by Thu?

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if helpful.

— Olivia Chen
Head of Product | Acme Insights
(External recipient)
